verses.english: Linked Discourses 17.3
Chapter One
A Turtle
At Sāvatthī.
“Possessions, honor, and popularity are grim …

verses.pali: Bhūtapubbaṁ, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṁ udakarahade mahākummakulaṁ ciranivāsi ahosi.
verses.english: Once upon a time in a certain lake there was a large family of turtles that had lived there for a long time.

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, aññataro kummo aññataraṁ kummaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then one of the turtles said to another,

verses.pali: ‘mā kho tvaṁ, tāta kumma, etaṁ padesaṁ agamāsī’ti.
verses.english: ‘My dear turtle, don’t you go to that place.’

verses.pali: Agamāsi kho, bhikkhave, so kummo taṁ padesaṁ.
verses.english: But that turtle did go to that place,
and a hunter pierced her with a harpoon.

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, so kummo yena so kummo tenupasaṅkami.
verses.english: Then that turtle went back to the other turtle.

verses.pali: Addasā kho, bhikkhave, so kummo taṁ kummaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
verses.english: When the other turtle saw her coming off in the distance,
he said,

verses.pali: ‘kacci tvaṁ, tāta kumma, na taṁ padesaṁ agamāsī’ti?
verses.english: ‘My dear turtle, I hope you didn’t go to that place!’
‘I did.’
‘But my dear turtle, I hope you’re not hurt or injured!’

verses.pali: ‘Akkhato khomhi, tāta kumma, anupahato, atthi ca me idaṁ suttakaṁ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhan’ti.
verses.english: ‘I’m not hurt or injured. But this cord keeps dragging behind me.’
‘Indeed, my dear turtle, you’re hurt and injured!

verses.pali: Etena hi te, tāta kumma, suttakena pitaro ca pitāmahā ca anayaṁ āpannā byasanaṁ āpannā.
verses.english: Your father and grandfather met with tragedy and disaster because of such a cord.

verses.pali: Gaccha dāni tvaṁ, tāta kumma, na dāni tvaṁ amhākan’ti.
verses.english: Go now, you are no longer one of us.’

verses.pali: Luddoti kho, bhikkhave, mārassetaṁ pāpimato adhivacanaṁ.
verses.english: ‘Hunter’ is a term for Māra the Wicked.
‘Harpoon’ is a term for possessions, honor, and popularity.
‘Cord’ is a term for greed and relishing.

verses.pali: Yo hi koci, bhikkhave, bhikkhu uppannaṁ lābhasakkārasilokaṁ assādeti nikāmeti—
verses.english: Whoever enjoys and likes arisen possessions, honor, and popularity is called a mendicant who has been pierced with a harpoon. They’ve met with tragedy and disaster, and the Wicked One can do with them what he wants.

verses.pali: ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu giddho papatāya anayaṁ āpanno byasanaṁ āpanno yathākāmakaraṇīyo pāpimato.

verses.english: So grim are possessions, honor, and popularity. …”
